info.title: doublegate organization gate
info.description:
The one inbound HTTP surface of an organization gate (ADR-0033) as ADR-0082 leaves it: one port, plaintext behind the operator's TLS terminator, and one question at every door — what ROLE is calling. A person signs in through OpenID Connect at the deployment group's issuer and presents that token; a program presents an opaque `dgk_` API key. Either way the credential resolves to one of four ranked roles, `reader` < `agent` < `reviewer` < `admin` (AUTH-4), and each route below names the one it needs in `x-role`. In `[surface] mode = local` the same route table is served keyless on loopback only, as the daemon owner (`uid:<n>`), and an off-loopback bind is refused at startup.

What this surface is not: a way to promote. Admission is the quorum's, on the socket, by a reviewer; the wire carries submissions in and outcomes out (ADR-0030 §3: the answer never rides the PUT).
x-invariants: INV-SEC-8: in key mode no data route answers without a valid credential; 401 is identical for no key and a forged key
INV-SEC-9: keys never appear in logs; the raw key is returned once, at issue
I1: /memories never reaches quarantine or the inbox
I2: the writer of an introduced claim is the credential's identity, never a field
AUTH-4: an agent reaches nothing above its row, on any transport — the gate is not callable by the thing being gated

bearer.description: `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` — a `dgk_` API key, or a person's JWT from the deployment group's issuer. The ROLE is a property of the credential, never of the request (AUTH-1, AUTH-3)

Envelope.description: The frozen v1 envelope (ADR-0022). Optional fields use canonical omission — an absent `derives_from` and an empty one must hash identically, so `[]` is never emitted.

content_hash.description: bare sha256 hex of the content bytes

SubmissionEvent.description: The whole-document commitment (`doublegate_sdk.submission.SubmissionEvent`). Its canonical bytes, hashed, are the submission's identity — **not** the envelope digest, which is the local production reference the attribution statements bind to. The two are never conflated.

review_refs.description: digest references to retained local records; the gate resolves them to exact bytes, it does not trust them

SignedSubmission.description: The event transport profile the SDK writes and `_put_authenticated_submission` parses (`doublegate_sdk.submission._parse_submission`). A closed field set: any unlisted member is refused. Identity is UNTRUSTED at parse time — the receiver re-parses the exact bytes and owns every authority check.

artifact_id.description: the signed submission's own identity — `document`'s canonical hash, prefixed. It must equal the path's artifact id (which is accepted bare or prefixed). Never the envelope digest.

signature.description: unpadded base64url Ed25519 over the domain-separated canonical event; 64 raw bytes

content.description: utf-8 text, or canonical RFC 4648 base64 when `encoding` is given

encoding.description: the only explicit encoding; omit for utf-8

space.description: a valid Unicode identifier; compared against the signed retained scope

local_verdicts.description: the client gate's own verdict records — evidence on the row, never authority here

local_promotion.description: the client's signed promote record, resolved against retained bytes

production_evidence_manifest.description: its digest must match the event's `evidence_manifest_digest`

on_behalf_of.description: the upstream principal a hop names (ADR-0082 d7, AUTH-5). Recorded on the journal line under that name and confers nothing: the role that decides this request is the presenting credential's.

LegacySubmission.description: The original inbox body, served when no signed-submission backend is installed behind this surface. The door verifies `local_promotion`'s signature against the key's deployment.

local_promotion.description: the client's signed promote event; the door verifies the signature against the key's deployment

Submission.description: Two bodies are documented because two are served, and which one applies is a property of the deployment, not of the request. A gate with an authenticated submission backend installed accepts only `SignedSubmission`; a gate without one accepts only `LegacySubmission`. `GET /openapi.json` on the gate you are talking to does not currently distinguish them — read the gate's configuration, not this document, to know which mode is bound.

Status.description: What `GET /status` answers: the inbox gauges (FR-45) plus, where an automatic review pipeline is configured, `org_review`.

depth.description: rows the inbox is holding right now

max_depth.description: the configured bound; `PUT /submissions` answers 503 at it

revision.description: the assembling commit (ADR-0051); `""` on a source checkout

done.description: count by outcome for finished rows; the key `""` is an unrecorded outcome

held.description: count by hold reason for `held_for_review` rows; `unstated` where none was recorded

OrgReviewStatus.description: Operator-visible automatic review *state*: never authority, never a credential. Only `enabled` and `blocked` are guaranteed — a store error is reported as the degraded form (`enabled`, `blocked: true`, `last_failure`) with a fixed reason, because a DSN can ride an exception message.

blocked.description: a blocked pipeline row, or a startup configuration refusal

counts.description: `queued` is pending_review + assessed + approved: everything the worker still owes a step

worker.description: the effective worker configuration, with nothing secret in it

model.description: the review backend's name, null when unbound

last_failure.description: the last recorded failure; `reason` is truncated and fixed-form, never an exception message

ClaimsGraphNode.description: One artifact in the projection. INV-SEC-10 lives in this shape: `label` (the body's head, 80 chars) is present only for `ACTIVE`/`SUPERSEDED` rows, and `source_uri` is null for every other state — a held artifact crosses as its existence and provenance attribution, never its content.

state.description: the limbo projection's state, e.g. ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, HELD, REJECTED

writer_label.description: the issuing key's label, joined at read; null for non-key writers

label.description: the body's head — serialized ONLY for ACTIVE/SUPERSEDED, absent otherwise (INV-SEC-10)

source_uri.description: null unless the row is ACTIVE/SUPERSEDED

banned.description: the admission bans matching this row's writer or source prefix. Matched internally, so a source ban is reported even where `source_uri` itself is withheld. Retention, not removal.

ClaimsGraph.description: The ADR-0035 relation projection serialized (FR-58): a pure function of the stores — nodes off limbo's projection, edges and pins off the graph's. Nothing is computed for the browser that `rebuild` would not reproduce.

edges.description: only recorded relations; ordered by ts then event_id

pins.description: tip overrides: an operator's pinned head for a supersession root

bans.description: every admission ban in effect, whether or not a node matches it

params.description: the verb's declared parameters (I7: an undeclared field is refused)

Approval.description: `dg.approval`: who approved, or why the row waits — a read model folded from the journal, never a state

own.description: authored by the presenting key (dg.node only)

ClaimNode.description: `dg.node`: one claim for a review surface. `preview` is the MASKED rendering, bounded (INV-SEC-7), null when the content is erased or the blob is gone.

status.description: the annotated status row: state, quorum, blocking, decisions, self_authored

items.description: a signed journal line: `countersign` or `refuse`, payload content-free

next.description: the position to ask from next

provenance.description: verbatim from the record: writer, source_uri, derives_from, signers — plus writer_label (the key's issuing label, joined at read; null for non-key writers) and ingest_ts (FR-65)

skill_ref.description: a URL fetched under skillref's bounds, instead of content

KeyRecord.description: One key as `GET /keys` and `dg.keys` render it. A role and nothing else grants: the `scopes` and `spaces` lists ADR-0033 gave a key are deleted (ADR-0082 d4/d5). Revoked and expired rows still render — the record is history, not a credential — and the hash never leaves (INV-SEC-9).

key_id.description: the first 12 hex characters of the key's sha256

bind.description: FR-51's client-gate deployment binding, present only on a key issued with one. A binding, never an authority: it says whose `local_promotion` this key may carry, never what the key may do

KeyRequest.description: What `POST /keys` takes. A key's role never exceeds its creator's (ADR-0082 d4), and the deployment binding is not self-service over the wire — an operator sets it where the key is minted.

expires_in_days.description: omit for a key that never expires; out of range is a 400, never a coerced value

put.summary: Submit an admitted claim to the organization's inbox (ADR-0030).

200.description: already held, or already decided — the state says which

401.description: no key, a forged key, an expired or revoked key — indistinguishable on purpose (INV-SEC-8, no oracle)

403.description: a live credential whose role is below the one this route needs (AUTH-4): it already proved it is real, so the reason is given

422.description: the key is fine; the BODY does not pass. A drain does not stop on this. The body carries a stable `code` from one of two disjoint namespaces. `SUBMISSION_*` — the P1-A submission contract (§4) — says the body is not a well-formed submission: `SUBMISSION_FIELD_MISSING`, `SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN_FIELD`, `SUBMISSION_ENCODING_INVALID`, `SUBMISSION_ARTIFACT_ID_MISMATCH`, checked in that fixed order so a body breaking two rules always names the earlier one. `ADMISSION_*` — the door (FR-51 / ADR-0034 §4) — says the body is well formed but this caller is not admitted (unsigned promotion, wrong deployment, no `local_promotion`, ungranted space): `ADMISSION_ROLE_TOO_LOW`, `ADMISSION_ROLE_NOT_CLIENT`, `ADMISSION_PROMOTION_MISSING`, `ADMISSION_PROMOTION_MALFORMED`, `ADMISSION_PROMOTION_NOT_PROMOTE`, `ADMISSION_PROMOTION_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `ADMISSION_DEPLOYMENT_UNBOUND`, `ADMISSION_ARTIFACT_UNBOUND`, `ADMISSION_SUBMISSION_MALFORMED`, `ADMISSION_SPACE_INVALID`, `ADMISSION_SPACE_MISMATCH`, `ADMISSION_REFUSED`. DEFINED BUT NOT YET REACHABLE: `SUBMISSION_CONTRACT_UNSUPPORTED`, `SUBMISSION_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `SUBMISSION_MEMBERSHIP_UNVERIFIED`, `SUBMISSION_MEMBERSHIP_STALE` are part of the contract's fixed verification order and will be emitted at the position they hold in it, but the submission wire format does not yet carry the members they are checked against. Their absence from a response means the check has not run — never that it ran and passed.

409.description: secure receipt backend only: this attempt key was already recorded with *different* bytes — the idempotency key is bound, not the body

500.description: secure receipt backend only: an internal receipt failure; the message is deliberately fixed, never the exception

put.description: Two bodies, one route, chosen by what is installed behind this surface (see `Submission`): a gate with an authenticated submission backend takes the SDK's closed-field signed event profile (`document`, `signature`, `artifact_id`, `content`, `space`, `local_verdicts`, `local_promotion`, `production_evidence_manifest`); a gate without one takes the legacy envelope + `local_promotion` body. The path's artifact id is the *submission event*'s identity — the canonical event hash, bare hex or `sha256:`-prefixed — never the envelope digest, which is the local production reference the attribution statements bind to. The door (ADR-0034 §4): the key must be bound to the deployment that signed. The answer never rides this request — the verdict is a `countersign` or `refuse` event, pulled from `GET /outcomes`. Idempotent by artifact id.

parameters.description: bare sha256 hex; the `sha256:` prefix is accepted and stripped

Only the content-independent causes — an unobtainable pin, a quarantined journal, a gap past its deadline — are declared truthfully as 409.

get.description: A pure function of the stores: nothing is computed for the browser that `rebuild` would not reproduce. INV-SEC-10 lives in the node shape — `label` (the body's head) and `source_uri` are serialized only for `ACTIVE`/`SUPERSEDED` rows, so a held artifact crosses as id, state, type, class, space, age and its provenance *attribution*, never its content. `writer_label` is the issuing key's label joined at read; `banned` is admission policy matched internally, so a source ban is reported even where the source itself is withheld. get.summary: The operator's bounded, read-only telemetry query (C-OBS). Admin only; `501` unless the operator configured a backend.

200.description: quarantined evidence; secret-shaped fields are dropped before the rows leave this process

400.description: out of bounds or malformed, to an authorized admin only: unknown signal, window over the ceiling, limit over the ceiling, non-integer window

404.description: not_available — the uniform withhold, and the ONLY answer an unauthorized caller gets: no key, a forged key, an expired or revoked key, and a live key without admin are byte-identical to each other and to a path that does not exist

501.description: no telemetry backend is configured behind this surface; reachable only after a genuine admin key has authenticated

502.description: the backend did not answer; the message is fixed and names no host, port, path or product

get.description: OPERATOR material, not tenant material: no org-space → telemetry-service mapping exists, so the readable set is the operator's configured allowlist and nothing else. There is no caller-supplied filter, expression or query parameter — the only caller-chosen string is `service`, admitted solely by exact membership in that allowlist, and the wire filter is assembled server-side from it. Read-only: nothing is written to the backend. **Unauthorized is a non-disclosure.** Every caller that is not an admin — no key, a forged key, an expired or revoked key, or a live credential below `admin` — receives the surface's uniform `404 not_available`, byte-identical to the answer for a path that does not exist. There is no `401` and no `403` on this route: a status that varied with the credential would tell an unauthorized caller that a guarded operator route lives at this path. This listing describes the shape of the service and is not an authorization rule — being documented here does not license a route to name itself while refusing. The backend (its URL, its token, its allowlist) is operator configuration carried on the daemon, never a request field; while it is unset this route answers `501`, which is the disabled-diagnostic state and is reachable only AFTER a genuine admin key has authenticated. Rows come back under an explicit `untrusted` flag: a log body is attacker-supplied text quoted as evidence, never instruction to a reader. Bounds are ceilings and are refused, not clamped — a silently shortened window makes a partial answer read as a complete one.

parameters.description: must be an exact member of the operator's configured allowlist

parameters.name: end_ms
parameters.description: epoch ms; the window has a 6h ceiling

parameters.name: time_aggregation
parameters.description: metrics only; `rate`/`increase` can read as an empty answer

post.description: Identity is the presenting credential (`uid:<n>` of the daemon owner in local mode), never a field. The route carries every verb, so its own floor is the lowest role any verb needs — `reader` — and each verb is then held to the role its catalog entry names, refused by name as `-32602` (AUTH-4). `dg.describe` answers the org catalog, so a console probes capabilities with one call. get.description: Requires the `reviewer` role in key mode (AUTH-4: it is the routing read for the people who review); local mode retains the loopback-only keyless contract. Authorization precedes query parsing. Only held_for_review submissions in a current eligible state count; org-local pending rows do not. Unknown hold reasons are unstated. Order is received_at then artifact_id. Total is the filtered routing-view count. Revision binds only this metadata view, not policy, content or authority. On 409 discard all accumulated pages and restart without a cursor. No bodies, sources, notes or evidence. Only single limit and cursor parameters are accepted; unknown or duplicate parameters fail.
